headline: Pilbara Minerals hammered 8.6% on a fresh lithium price collapse — the ASX held up otherwise, and Meta's new AI models are taking on OpenAI head-to-head.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Brutal session for PLS — China's lithium carbonate futures plunged nearly 12% and hit a 10-month low, with institutions warning of a 2027 oversupply glut. That hammered sentiment across all lithium miners, and PLS copped the full force of it today.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped last night, weighed down by some negative noise around GTA 6 — a hacker ('CyberLeek') is threatening to post the entire game story online unless Rockstar releases a physical disc version. Not a fundamental issue, more headline-driven jitter ahead of what remains a massive upcoming release.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI dipped slightly today in a mild pullback for AI-related stocks on the ASX. Nothing stock-specific; the broader AI theme remains intact with Meta's major new model launch this week keeping the sector in focus.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE eased modestly today, likely reflecting some caution around the IMF's warnings about global growth risks and ongoing Middle East tensions which tend to weigh on emerging market sentiment.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft had a solid night last night, up over 1%. The market is warming up ahead of Microsoft's October 28 earnings, with analysts focused on Azure cloud growth and the AI Maia 300 chip reducing costs. Strong momentum heading into results.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google edged higher last night ahead of its Q3 2026 earnings. Analysts are flagging it as a quality growth stock with high returns on invested capital, and the market seems to be positioning ahead of the print.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG barely moved today — a tiny dip of 0.17% that's well within normal daily noise for a diversified fund. Nothing to read into here.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS edged down slightly today, tracking a mild overnight pullback in US markets. The S&P 500 and NASDAQ were both marginally lower last night, but nothing alarming — this is normal day-to-day movement for a broad US index fund.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Lithium rout continues, hold your nerve
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals dropped 8.6% today after Chinese lithium carbonate futures crashed nearly 12% to a 10-month low. Institutions are warning of a 2027 oversupply. PLS is already down 54% from your cost base — a brutal run. But selling now locks in that loss. The long-term case for lithium in the energy transition is still real, just delayed. Sit tight unless you genuinely need the capital.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Earnings on Oct 28, momentum building
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is up 1.09% last night and the market is building anticipation ahead of its October 28 earnings report. Azure cloud growth and AI cost-cutting via the new Maia 300 chip are the key storylines. You're up 23% on this position — strong long-term hold. If there's any pre-earnings dip, that could be a chance to top up.

watch_today.title: GOOG — Q3 earnings approaching, stock ticking up
watch_today.detail: Alphabet rose 0.72% last night with earnings on the horizon. Analysts are pointing to its durable growth profile and strong returns on capital. You're up 14% on your position. Nothing to do here — just keep an eye on the earnings date. Long-term story remains solid.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 hacker threat is noise, not a structural issue
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell 2.57% last night after a hacker threatened to leak the entire GTA 6 storyline online. This is headline drama, not a reason to rethink the investment. GTA 6 is still one of the most anticipated game launches in history, with a PC release planned for early 2027. You're down 12% overall — hold and wait for the launch catalyst.

watch_today.title: IMF warns global economy is near its 'limits of resilience'
watch_today.detail: The IMF's annual World Economic Outlook flagged risks from AI market corrections, war, and rising global debt. Australia specifically was called out for having some of the worst inflation and unemployment trajectories among developed nations. Worth watching — if these risks materialise, emerging markets (VGE) and growth ETFs (VDHG) could face headwinds.

watch_today.title: Middle East tensions lifting oil — keep an eye on inflation
watch_today.detail: Houthi rebels are escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia, killing 1 and injuring 11 in the latest strike on a Saudi airport. Oil is sitting at US$93.89/barrel. If this escalates further and oil spikes, it feeds directly into Australian inflation — which the RBA is already struggling to control. Bad news for rate cut hopes.

world.summary: The big global stories today centre on the US midterms, escalating Middle East conflict, and the IMF's stark warning that the global economy is approaching its limits.

stories.title: Elon Musk spends $366m backing Republicans ahead of US midterms
stories.why_it_matters: Elon Musk has poured a staggering $366 million into supporting the Republican Party ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections — one of the largest single-donor political investments in American history. At the same time, the Trump administration has reportedly decided to skip international election observers for the midterms, a move that watchdog groups say undermines democratic accountability. A federal judge has also ordered a temporary halt to taxpayer-funded pro-Trump TV ads. The midterms will determine control of Congress and have huge implications for US economic and foreign policy.

stories.title: Houthis escalate attacks on Saudi Arabia as Middle East conflict widens
stories.why_it_matters: Iran-backed Houthi rebels launched another attack on a Saudi airport, killing 1 person and injuring 11. The attacks are increasing in frequency and scale as the broader Middle East conflict drags on. Australia's government has issued a high degree of caution warning for Middle East travel. Oil prices remain elevated at around US$94/barrel partly on these tensions, and analysts warn the entire LNG (liquefied natural gas) industry in the region remains at risk while the Iran-linked conflict continues.

stories.title: IMF warns global economy 'could soon test the limits of resilience'
stories.why_it_matters: The IMF's annual World Economic Outlook, released at its Annual Meetings today, delivered a sobering message: the global economy is approaching the limits of its resilience. The Fund flagged three big risks — a potential AI stock market correction (think of it like the dot-com bubble popping), ongoing wars disrupting trade and energy, and dangerously high government debt levels in major economies. For everyday Australians, this means higher borrowing costs and slower growth could stick around longer than hoped.

stories.title: Rep. Ilhan Omar's home searched by federal agents in criminal probe
stories.why_it_matters: Federal agents searched the home of Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar as part of a criminal investigation. No charges have been announced yet, but the development is significant given Omar is a prominent progressive voice in Congress. The move comes amid a broader political environment where federal agencies are being used in ways critics say are politically motivated, adding to tensions heading into the midterms.

stories.title: Immigration front and centre as US midterms approach
stories.why_it_matters: Immigration is shaping up as the defining issue of the 2026 US midterms, with voters split on whether Trump's crackdowns have gone too far. The Guardian's reporting finds many Hispanic communities — traditionally a swing vote — increasingly alienated by the administration's approach. How Congress swings on immigration will affect trade policy, visa rules, and potentially even Australian student and worker visa arrangements down the track.

markets.summary: The ASX had a decent session today, up 0.76% to close at 8,783. Last night in the US, both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ edged lower — the S&P fell 0.16% and the NASDAQ dropped 0.24%. Oil is holding firm above US$93 on Middle East tensions, gold is steady near US$4,188, and the Aussie dollar firmed slightly to about 69.9 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Good day on the local market, up 0.76%.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Marginal dip last night — markets treading water ahead of US earnings season.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Slight pullback last night despite strength in MSFT and GOOG.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil holding elevated levels on Houthi attacks and Middle East risk.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Barely moved — gold staying near record highs as a safe haven.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar nudging higher, close to 70 US cents.

politics.summary: The RBA and interest rates dominated Australian news today, with the IMF also calling out Australia specifically for having some of the worst inflation and unemployment trends in the developed world. Parliament also passed new university access legislation.

stories.title: RBA minutes reveal door still open to further rate hikes
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank's latest board minutes made clear that further interest rate rises remain on the table if inflation doesn't cool fast enough. The RBA has flagged it's prepared to accept weaker economic growth as the price of beating inflation — which means mortgage holders shouldn't bank on rate cuts any time soon. A former RBA governor pushed back, saying the hikes 'won't change much' because inflation is being driven by supply-side issues the RBA can't control with higher rates.

stories.title: IMF singles out Australia for worst inflation and rising unemployment
stories.why_it_matters: The IMF's World Economic Outlook specifically called out Australia as one of the worst performers among developed nations on both inflation and rising unemployment. That's a double whammy — prices are still too high, and more people are losing jobs. For everyday Australians, this means the cost-of-living squeeze is likely to continue, and the job market may get tougher before it gets better.

stories.title: Parliament passes legislation to help more Australians access university
stories.why_it_matters: Legislation has passed Parliament aimed at making university more accessible for more Australians — details on the specific measures (such as fee changes or HECS reform) weren't available in the article text, but the passage signals the government is pushing ahead with its higher education agenda. This is part of Labor's broader effort to widen participation in tertiary education.

ai.summary: Meta made a huge splash by launching two new frontier AI models — Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full — claiming they match OpenAI and Anthropic. Meanwhile, regulators globally are sharpening their focus on AI oversight, and the debate over how to govern AI is getting louder.

stories.title: Meta launches Muse Wonder — says it matches OpenAI and Anthropic
stories.why_it_matters: Meta has released two new AI models called Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, claiming benchmark results that put them on par with the best models from OpenAI (ChatGPT) and Anthropic (Claude). Muse Wonder Full — the more powerful version — introduces 'Active Memory' and 'Active Focus' features, meaning it can remember things across conversations and zoom in on what matters most. The catch: only the weaker Muse Wonder model is available via the API (the programming interface developers use to build apps), while Wonder Full is reserved for Meta's own products. A subscription tier is reportedly priced at US$200/month, putting it squarely in premium territory.

stories.title: UK restores frontier AI model testing deal — here's how it works
stories.why_it_matters: The UK has restored its deal with major AI labs to test their most powerful 'frontier' models (the cutting-edge systems like GPT-5 or Muse Wonder Full) before they're released to the public. The UK AI minister outlined how it works: companies share early access with government safety testers who look for dangerous capabilities. This is the kind of pre-release safety check that doesn't exist in most countries — including Australia — and the debate over whether it should is growing.

stories.title: Key financial watchdogs signal they'll step up AI regulation
stories.why_it_matters: Major financial regulators — including the Financial Stability Board (FSB), which coordinates global financial rules — are signalling they'll ramp up oversight of how AI is used in financial markets and banking. The FSB is also turning its attention to stablecoins (digital currencies pegged to real-world assets like the US dollar). For investors, this means AI companies operating in finance could face new compliance costs, and crypto-adjacent investments could see new rules soon.

stories.title: IMF flags AI market correction as a top global risk
stories.why_it_matters: The IMF has explicitly named a potential AI stock market correction as one of the top three risks to the global economy. In plain English: AI stocks have run very hard, and if the hype doesn't translate into real profits fast enough, a sharp sell-off is possible — similar to the dot-com crash of the early 2000s. This is directly relevant to holdings like GXAI and GOOG, both of which are heavily exposed to AI valuations.

sport.summary: The Rugby League World Cup is the dominant sports story as Australia gears up for the tournament, with plenty of team tips and squad intrigue. The AFL trade period is also in full swing with 72 hours to go.

stories.title: Kalyn Ponga responds to big switch rumour; Kangaroos captain reveals Walsh shock — World Cup team tips
stories.why_it_matters: Kalyn Ponga has responded to rumours he could switch codes or clubs ahead of the Rugby League World Cup, while the Kangaroos captain has weighed in on the selection surprise around Reece Walsh. Team tips for the World Cup are coming thick and fast as squads finalise — the tournament is shaping up as one of the biggest RL events in years.

stories.title: Full 2026 Rugby League World Cup schedule and how it works
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports has published the full schedule for the 2026 Rugby League World Cup, explaining the format and how the tournament progresses from group stage through to the final. If you're planning to watch or follow along, this is your go-to reference for dates, times, and the structure of the competition.

stories.title: Carlton land Lachie Whitfield in major AFL trade with GWS Giants
stories.why_it_matters: Carlton have secured midfielder Lachie Whitfield from the GWS Giants in what's shaping up as one of the bigger trades of the AFL trade period. Whitfield is an elite ball-winner who adds class and experience to Carlton's midfield. With 72 hours left in the trade window, more deals are expected before the deadline.

stories.title: World Cup breakout stars to watch — from Haas protege to gun who could shake up Dogs halves
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports has identified the breakout players to watch at the Rugby League World Cup — including a Haas family protege and a halfback who could reshape the Canterbury Bulldogs' plans. These are the young guns who could make their names on the biggest stage in international league this year.

stories.title: Championship Tour surfer suspended after accusations of 'a deeply serious nature'
stories.why_it_matters: A surfer on the WSL Championship Tour — the top tier of professional surfing — has been suspended following accusations described as being 'of a deeply serious nature.' No further details were given in the report, and the surfer's name was not publicly released. Given the Gold Coast's strong surf culture, this will likely attract local interest as more details emerge.
